newsitem.title: UK: Korean merchant banks face more competition - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Korean merchant banks face more competition - S&P.

text.p: The Korean merchant banking industry will see competition further intensify with the entrance of 15 finance companies that converted to merchant banks in July 1996, Standard & Poor's said on Thursday.
"At the same time, profitability in the industry has been diminishing," said S&P in a statement, adding that this trend will worsen with the recent addition of the new participants.

S&P said that although the top-tier merchant banks are only one-tenth the size of large Korean commercial banks, six traditional players have carved out profitable niches in areas such as commercial paper discounting, leasing, and foreign currency lending.

"The largest merchant banks have taken advantage of flexibility afforded by comparatively lenient regulation and the absence of reserve requirements that burden Korea's commercial banks," the rating agency said.
Merchant banks have grown rapidly and so far have been profitable, building capital along the way, S&P said.
However, S&P said the merchant banks face serious risks, and sustaining strong performance levels will depend on the nimbleness of individual managements.
"Each of the merchant banks' business niches is subject to sharply increasing competition, whether from the new entrants or from commercial banks and their subsidiaries," the agency said.
The merchant banks' small size and lesser importance to corporate clients compared with the commercial banks leaves them particularly vulnerable, S&P noted.
It said rapid growth, combined with substantial exposures to the large corporate groups (chaebols) were particular problems.
S&P said asset quality could deteriorate rapidly at some merchant banks, as it has at some of the smaller players.

Over the medium term, Standard & Poor's said the industry would consolidated because of a widening gap between strong and weak players, and as a result of pressure on individual participants' financial parameters.
"Industrial groups' interests in retaining controlling ownership of merchant banks, however, will be an obstacle to consolidation," S&P said.
